text:
jessica: Hey team, incoming from a large customer — their service is seeing an increase in 5xx counts for streaming endpoints. They say the client frequently gets a socket error and we log a 5xx. They provided curl logs and app stack traces.
jessica: TL;DR: intermittent EPIPE / ECONNRESET on client -> our gateway during long streaming responses, but those client disconnects are showing up as 5xx in metrics and triggering paging. Billing also spiked because we counted tokens as failed requests.

mike: can you paste the curl logs / request flow? which endpoint and protocol (http1/2) are they using?

jessica: They use HTTP/1.1 chunked streaming from a fleet of node clients. Example repro command:

jessica: ```
$ curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streaming/generate
```

jessica: Client sees: "curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer". On our side the gateway logs show an upstream error and we emit a 502/500 at the API layer.

samir: do we have the gateway logs for that exact request id? any upstream (runtime) crash or just socket close?

jessica: Customer included one request id: r-0a1b2c3d. Gateway shows: `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream` and then we map that to 502. Runtime logs for that timeframe show normal generation, no exception; tail shows last token streamed then connection closed.

lina: this sounds like client abort after server wrote last chunk. Historically we've had two failure classes: 1) true server 5xx (runtime crash/timeout), 2) client aborts that look like EPIPE/ECONNRESET and get classified as 5xx by the gateway. The latter should not be charged as server failures.

mike: agreed. need to confirm whether kernel-level ECONNRESET originates from client or from an intermediate (load balancer idle timeout). What's the idle timeout on the path?

jessica: customer is behind a mobile SDK, sometimes the app backgrounding kills the socket immediately. They say it’s common. They provided a packet capture showing FIN from client ~50ms after final chunk.

samir: ok, that points to client-initiated close. Our gateway currently treats any upstream connection close without a 2xx as 5xx. We should change classification: if runtime completed and sent last chunk but connection closed by client, mark metric as client-abort (499-like) not 5xx.

mike: Dev plan: 1) adjust gateway to examine runtime completion flag and socket errno (EPIPE/EINVAL/etc). If runtime indicates successful completion (no exception and output closed cleanly), emit 499/CLIENT_ABORT vs 502. 2) update billing pipeline to exclude client-aborts from failure billing. 3) add logs and metric tag "client_abort=true" for visibility.

lina: also check chunked encoding edgecases — some clients don't read final zero-length chunk if they close midstream, and some proxies will respond with RST that we might be interpreting as upstream reset. We need to record whether the last write failed with EPIPE or whether the runtime encountered broken pipe while writing.

jessica: I captured runtime trace: runtime returned success (exit code 0), wrote N tokens, closed its stdout. Then gateway attempted to flush to client and got EPIPE.

samir: that's perfect repro. So we can detect runtime success and then classify the gateway EPIPE as client-abort.

mike: quick patch idea: when we get an EPIPE on write, check the request context for runtime_done==true. If true, increment metric client_abort and return no-error for rate-of-server-errors. Don't increment server_5xx. Also tag request logs with "client_eof=true".

jessica: will that change existing alerting? Pager currently triggers on 5xx spike. We should update alert to ignore spikes where >80% of 5xx are client_abort-tagged.

lina: yes, update SLO/alert rule. Also add an automated sample link for those requests so SRE can quickly see traces.

samir: one caution: if runtime success but client aborted before receiving final chunk (e.g., not all tokens flushed), we might overcount delivered tokens. Billing should only charge for tokens actually sent to the client, not tokens produced by runtime but never transmitted. How are we calculating token billing currently?

mike: current pipeline charges tokens counted at runtime output. We do not currently reconcile with bytes written to socket. That mismatch explains customer's billing surprise.

jessica: for now we need two fixes: immediate: stop classifying client abort as server 5xx (to silence pages) and stop counting aborted requests as failures in SLA. medium: change billing to bill based on bytes actually transmitted (or at least mark aborted sessions so we can refund/adjust).

lina: for repro, customer willing to run a small test. They can reproduce quickly by backgrounding the app mid-stream. They shared a small Node snippet:

lina: ```js
const req = fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer X' } });
setTimeout(() => { // simulate app backgrounding
  req.abort();
}, 1200);
```

jessica: we asked them to run this while we flip a tracing flag. They did and provided the trace. I uploaded it to the support ticket.

samir: next steps and owners:
- mike: implement gateway classification change + metric tag (PR target EOD).
- lina: update alerting to ignore client_abort-heavy spikes + add dashboard card.
- billing-eng: (cc @finance) please investigate token billing reconciliation and flag for refunds if needed.
- jessica: coordinate with customer and collect a couple more traces.

mike: quick note on implementation detail: we should avoid relying solely on errno strings — use layered checks: runtime_success boolean, bytes_written vs bytes_generated, and socket-level errno. Also add a short delay to allow runtime to close before marking abort, to avoid race with legitimate upstream crashes.

jessica: I'm going to mark this high priority for the support queue and escalate billing. customer is ok with a workaround if we can mute paging and do a follow-up billing credit.

deploy-bot: Deployed gateway patch candidate to staging cluster gke-staging at 2026-03-15T16:40:02Z for testing.

samir: once patch is in staging we'll run the customer's Node script against staging for validation. If passes, roll to prod with feature flag for 48h.

lina: also adding unit tests for chunked flush behavior and an integration test that simulates client RST/FIN patterns.

jessica: thanks team. I'll update the customer and keep the thread posted. :thumbsup:
